owner_steering: We are doing 200 AD; modern truck-handling studies are inappropriate for calibrating this setting.
supersedes: handling_observation_primary.json as the active next task. Keep that historical declaration and the FAO screen unchanged; the modern observational study is discontinued with no rate, staff or model adoption.
target: Handling of grain in the Roman world around AD 200. Prefer dated documentary evidence from AD 100–300 (with exact date, location and occupation); identify earlier/later material explicitly as temporal transfer. Primary literary prescriptions are not measured productivity.
question: What do period sources actually establish about grain handling operations, loads, work organisation and any matched quantity/crew/time denominator?
source_rule: Begin with a bounded search for period papyri, inscriptions or directly identified ancient passages, supported by scholarly editions and translations. Record source date/site/material/operation and distinguish handling from long-distance transport or wages. No invented ancient task rates or automatic conversion of pay, storage volume or shipping duration into handler productivity.
stopping_rule: If a matched period work denominator is absent, retain handling rates as unknown. The existing annual atlas stays provisional. Do not substitute modern truck/conveyor throughput or rural crop-work slack to close the gap.
exclusions: No further modern handling-study extraction, ancient/fantasy coefficient adoption, staff recruitment, food/work/stock/graph solve, climate or atlas update in this evidence step.
